faqs.q: How do I answer "Why is there a gap in your resume?" in an interview?
faqs.a: Give a short, honest reason, mention what you did or learned during the break, and then explain why you are ready for this role now. For example, say you took time off to care for a family member, completed a certification during that period and are now keen to return full-time.

faqs.q: Is a one-year career gap a problem for getting a job?
faqs.a: Usually not, if you can explain it clearly. Many employers are comfortable with gaps of around a year, especially for reasons like health, family, further study or exam preparation, and longer gaps are easier to accept when you can show courses, freelance work or projects from that time.

faqs.q: Should I mention my career gap on my resume?
faqs.a: Yes, it is better to show it than to leave unexplained dates. Add a short entry such as Career Break or Planned Career Break with the dates and a line on what you did, such as courses, freelance work or caregiving. Breaks from many years ago usually do not need to be listed.

faqs.q: Can I hide a career gap by changing my job dates?
faqs.a: No, avoid changing dates or stretching a previous job to cover a gap. Background verification and experience or relieving letters can show the real dates, and being caught can cost you the offer, whereas an honest, confident explanation is usually accepted.
